summary.headline: Yasho Q2 FY27 revenue rose to INR347.92 crore (+89.5% YoY) and PAT to INR33.68 crore, but management flagged freight and energy costs squeezing margins.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR347.92 crore versus INR183.6 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR72.92 crore (up 118.2%) and PAT of INR33.68 crore versus INR4.86 crore. Management said volume grew 62% YoY and 7% QoQ, with capacity utilisation at 66%. The company absorbed about INR10 crore extra freight (Q1 to Q2 rise to INR20 crore) and INR1.8 crore higher gas costs, which management said it cannot pass on for accepted purchase orders. The company also announced a INR250 crore capex for two new buildings at Pakhajan, funded by INR100 crore internal accruals and INR150 crore sanctioned term loans.

segments.name: Industrial chemicals (lubricant additives and related)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 90% of revenue, per management. Product count rose from about 140 to about 152 products, with mix shifts cited as a key driver of realisations.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share about 70% of revenue in Q2 FY27, up from about 65% in Q1 FY27 and about 63% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin aspiration of at least 20-21%; management declined to commit to 23-24% for next year.
Utilisation expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27; FY27 utilisation previously guided near 70%, and management said H2 could reach about 80%.
Special contract (about INR120-150 crore, MNC) to start commercial supply in Q1 FY28 after trial production by Q4 FY27; INR120 crore received to date under the contract.
Special project expected to run at about 75% utilisation in FY28 and about 80-85% in FY29 (Phase 1).
Two new buildings (Phase 2, Pakhajan) expected commercial by late FY28 or early FY29, with 50-60% utilisation in first year.
Management expects to pass on freight and gas cost increases to customers from Q3 FY27 onwards, except for fixed-price contracts running to December.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue grew about 40% from Q4 FY26 while utilisation rose only 60% to 66%; how to split volume and price, and what drove gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 to Q2 volume grew 7% and value about 13%; H1 volume up about 73% YoY; prices up 10-15% since March from raw materials, rest from mix. Gross margin flat per management; EBITDA gain attributed to deleveraging of fixed costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise further as utilisation increases? Is 23-24% EBITDA possible next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to maintain EBITDA above 20-21% and declined to commit to 23-24%; said benefit of deleveraging may be passed to customers to grow business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall about 300 bps QoQ after last quarter's around 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 200 bps to freight and energy cost increases on contracts that could not be repriced, and about 100 bps to product mix; said it could not assure margins beyond 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for logistics and freight costs and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed contracts to December cannot be changed; spot business is repriced at current negotiated rates. Management could not forecast November-December freight.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR250 crore capex tied to customers, and what share of utilisation is covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Soft commitment from a customer covering about 50% of the new capacity's utilisation; capex is part of the lubricant-additive localisation strategy and partly incremental.

qa_highlights.question: Phase-wise utilisation expectations for FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Special project about 75% utilisation in FY28 and 80-85% in FY29; new buildings 50-60% in first year, then rising.

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook with the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to stay within limits, is well below 2.5x debt-to-EBITDA, and will set a comfort level at Board level; no ballpark for FY28-29 given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,600 crore target conservative, and is it based on current or pre-war prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is better to be conservative; the INR1,600 crore peak revenue figure was based on pre-war prices and assumes 80% utilisation within two quarters.

capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capacity utilisation 66% (vs about 60% in Q4 FY26 per analyst); management expects better utilisation in Q3 and Q4 FY27; FY27 utilisation previously guided near 70%.

Planned FY27 capex INR250 crores for two new manufacturing buildings at Pakhajan (Building 3 and 4), funded by INR100 crores internal accruals and INR150 crores sanctioned term loans; partly also equipment for Buildings 1 and 2.
Buildings 1 and 2 (existing) expected fully occupied and operational by end FY27 or Q1 FY28; Buildings 3 and 4 operational earliest Q4 FY28 or Q1 FY29.
Special contract (MNC, about INR120-150 crores): trial production by Q4 FY27, commercial supply Q1 FY28; INR120 crores received to date; expected about 75% utilisation in FY28, about 80-85% in FY29.

Phase 2 buildings: 50-60% utilisation in first year, rising thereafter; soft customer commitment covers about 50% of their utilisation; further capex needed to fill Buildings 3 and 4, to be discussed in January or April call.
Peak revenue from existing facilities about INR1,600 crores at 80% utilisation (based on pre-war prices, as of 30 March 2026 capex); management said it expects 80% achievable in next two quarters.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 volume up 62% YoY and 7% QoQ; value up about 13% QoQ; H1 FY27 volume growth about 73% YoY per management, revenue up 71.7% YoY.

Raw material prices up about 10-15% since March 2026 (mix of inputs, some up 100%, some zero); price increase attributed by management to raw materials, with product mix as the balance of revenue growth.

Freight cost rose from INR10 crores in Q1 FY27 to INR20 crores in Q2 FY27; gas price increase added INR1.8 crores; these were absorbed as accepted POs could not be repriced; fixed-price contracts run to December, spot business repriced at current rates.
Product count rose from about 140 to about 152; management said mix, not new products alone, drives realisations, and declined to say new products carry higher margins.
Export share about 70% in Q2 FY27 (about 65% Q1 FY27, about 63% FY26); management flagged customer resistance to high prices and switching to cheaper suppliers.

Management cites addressable market of about USD 15 billion; company revenue base about USD 100-120 million, with aspiration of USD 300-400 million over time; MNC localisation inquiries from global lubricant additive players.
risks_watch: Freight and logistics: shipments delayed 30-60 days versus a standard 25-30 days, vessel availability constraints and rising freight; management cannot forecast Nov-Dec freight.
Energy and raw material inflation: management warned further fuel or price rises could soften margins; raw material procurement challenging per management.
Pricing pressure: customers resisting high prices, some switching to cheaper suppliers; Q3 FY27 onward pass-through depends on contract terms.

Execution risk on the MNC special contract (trial by Q4 FY27, commercial supply Q1 FY28) and on the Pakhajan buildings (Phase 2 by late FY28 or early FY29); contract value and products under NDA and not disclosed.
Margin guidance is soft: management commits only to at least 20-21% EBITDA and declined 23-24% next year; watch whether H2 FY27 margins hold after pass-through.
key_quotes: We are ensuring that we get at least 20%-21% or something more than that, but that's our aspiration.
Demand is not slowing down. So that's one good sign for us. Demand is growing.
So we need to be cautious about passing on all the cost to customers because as you see, we are more into the export market rather than the domestic market.
It's better to be conservative than optimistic in today's scenario.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and demand, but cautious and evasive on margins and forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify FY28 margins, the size of the lubricant localisation opportunity, or the MNC contract value, citing NDA and volatility.

growth.why: Management guides FY28 revenue above Rs 1,600 crore and expects utilisation to rise from 66% toward 80% within two quarters, backed by Buildings 1-2 filling, a MNC special contract (INR120 crore received, commercial supply Q1 FY28), and price/mix gains; Phase 2 buildings (INR250 crore capex) only come online late FY28 with about 50% soft commitment, so the FY28 target rests on partly unverified de

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell about 300 bps QoQ to ~21% (about 200 bps from freight and energy), management will only commit to 20-21%, and declined to commit to 23-24% next year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Buildings 1 and 2 are expected fully operational by end FY27 or Q1 FY28, and the MNC special contract moves to commercial supply in Q1 FY28 after trial production by Q4 FY27; Buildings 3 and 4 follow only at Q4 FY28 or Q1 FY29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew 62% YoY and 7% QoQ with utilisation at 66%, and management expects utilisation to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27 toward about 80% within two quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 66%, below the 80% threshold, but INR250 crore is already committed and management said further capex to fill Buildings 3 and 4 will be discussed in the January or April call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY28 revenue at more than INR1,600 crore but cut the EBITDA margin wording to 'at least 20-plus%' and gave no upside on margins, while freight and gas costs remain unrecovered on fixed-price contracts to December.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight rose from INR10 crore to INR20 crore QoQ, management cannot forecast Nov-Dec freight, and fixed-price contracts run to December, so H2 margins could fall below 20% before pass-through takes effect from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: MNC special contract commercial supply
rows.why: Trial production by Q4 FY27 and commercial supply in Q1 FY28 on a ~INR120-150 crore contract, with INR120 crore already received and ~75% utilisation expected in FY28.

rows.label: Freight and gas pass-through from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects to pass on freight (INR20 crore in Q2) and gas (INR1.8 crore) increases from Q3 FY27, except fixed-price contracts running to December.

rows.label: Debt-to-EBITDA falling
rows.why: Debt-to-EBITDA fell to 2.09x in H1 FY27 from 3.74x in FY26, and management says it is well below the 2.5x comfort level even with capex.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, demand and the MNC contract, but cautious on margins, declining to commit beyond 20-21% EBITDA or 23-24% for next year; analysts pressed on the 300 bps QoQ margin fall, the freight pass-through and the phasing of Phase 2 utilisation.
